record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: In an appropriate sense, is the set of spacetime metrics that can be smoothly or distributionally extended across Cauchy horizons a measure-zero subset of all spacetimes?

evidence.quote: Show that, in an appropriate sense, the set of spacetime metrics which are (smoothly?, distributionally?) extendible across Cauchy horizons are "measure zero" in the set of all spacetimes ([ME;Ml], generally asked about spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ denote a suitable space of smooth globally hyperbolic spacetimes $(M,g)$ — for example, maximal globally hyperbolic developments of smooth vacuum (or otherwise suitably constrained) initial data on a compact Cauchy surface $\Sigma$, equipped with a natural topology (e.g., a Whitney/Sobolev-type topology on the space of initial data, or an analogous notion of "measure" or genericity such as a Baire-generic or prevalence notion).

Say that $(M,g) \in \mathcal{M}$ is *Cauchy-horizon extendible in regularity class $\mathcal{R}$* if there exists a connected Lorentzian manifold $(\widetilde{M},\widetilde{g})$ with $\widetilde{g}$ of regularity $\mathcal{R}$ (e.g., $C^\infty$ smooth, or merely distributional in the sense that $\widetilde{g}$ is locally bounded with weak derivatives in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ so that the Christoffel symbols and curvature make distributional sense) and an isometric embedding $\iota:(M,g)\hookrightarrow(\widetilde{M},\widetilde{g})$ such that $\iota(M)$ is a proper subset of $\widetilde{M}$ and $\partial \iota(M)$ contains a non-empty Cauchy horizon for $\iota(\Sigma)$.

Question: Show that, in an appropriate sense made precise by an explicit choice of topology and notion of "measure zero" (e.g., complement of a Baire-generic set, or measure zero with respect to a suitable measure on the space of initial data), the subset
$$\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{R}} \;=\; \{(M,g)\in\mathcal{M} : (M,g) \text{ is Cauchy-horizon extendible in regularity class } \mathcal{R}\}$$
is a "measure zero" subset of $\mathcal{M}$, both in the case $\mathcal{R}=C^\infty$ and in the case where $\mathcal{R}$ denotes a distributional regularity class.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a precise form of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture for spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces. The conjecture remains open in general; it has been formulated in both smooth (Penrose) and distributional/Christodoulou versions, and recent surveys (e.g., Van de Moortel 2025) describe partial results in symmetry classes (e.g., spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar-field, Reissner–Nordström interiors) and the Kerr Cauchy-horizon stability program, but no general proof of measure-zero/genericity of extendibility across Cauchy horizons is known.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture (Van de Moortel)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing the conjecture that generic maximal Cauchy developments are inextendible, with partial results in symmetry classes; the general problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The general strong cosmic censorship conjecture, in both smooth and distributional formulations, is still an open problem with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Strong cosmic censorship — Mihalis Dafermos
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjecture that generic Cauchy data lead to inextendible maximal developments and the role of Kerr Cauchy horizons.
status_evidence.claim: Genericity of Cauchy-horizon inextendibility is the content of strong cosmic censorship and remains conjectural.
